info.title: Vercel Blob
info.description:
The Vercel Blob data plane: uploads, heads, lists and deletes ride the API host, and blob content is served from a per-store subdomain.

THIS DOCUMENT IS AUTHORED, NOT VENDORED, like its sibling specs/vercel/kv.json. Vercel's published OpenAPI document describes blob-store management (create a store, change its access) and none of the data plane; the data plane is documented in prose and in the @vercel/blob SDK. What is transcribed here is the surface of the vendor-authored oracle, vercel-labs/emulate (pinned in specs/vercel/emulate-inventory.json), specifically packages/@emulators/vercel/src/routes/blob.ts -- its eight route registrations, its auth rule (a Bearer token of the form vercel_blob_rw_<prefix>_<storeId>_<suffix>, or an x-vercel-blob-store-id header when the Bearer token carries no store), and its exact response fields.

Two spellings in this document are mirror's, not any client's. GET /api/blob is one handler in the oracle, heading when ?url is present and listing otherwise; it is two path items here because an operation carries one response shape, and the ?url constraint is how the router tells them apart (a trailing-slash registration of the same handler needs no entry: routing trims it). And ServeBlob's response is an envelope that is not on the wire: the wire answer is the raw bytes plus ETag/Cache-Control/Content-Type headers, and the envelope's members are where a behavior bundle names those -- the codec unfolds it. The multipart routes are the oracle's own stubs: it answers every multipart call 400 bad_request, and so do the operations here.

servers.description: Vercel Blob API. Management calls ride this host; content is served from <storeId>.public.blob.vercel-storage.com, a per-store subdomain of this one.

put.summary: Upload a blob (or copy one, with ?fromUrl=)

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Where the blob lives. Absent is a 400 answered by the bundle, not a validation fault, because the oracle checks auth first.

parameters.name: fromUrl
parameters.description: Copy: the source blob's URL or pathname instead of a request body.

400.description: Bad pathname, unsupported access, or the blob exists and overwrite was not allowed.

403.description: No store could be resolved from the token or header.

404.description: A fromUrl copy source does not exist.

get.summary: List blobs, optionally folded by folder

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Arrives as a string like every query parameter; absent or unparsable means 1000.

get.summary: Head one blob by url or pathname
get.description: The oracle's GET handler heads when the url query parameter is present and lists otherwise; this path item is the head half, routed by the query constraint.

post.summary: Delete blobs by url or pathname

200.description: JSON null, whatever was or was not deleted.

412.description: The x-if-match ETag precondition failed on a targeted blob.

post.summary: The oracle does not support multipart uploads

400.description: Always: the oracle answers every multipart call 400 bad_request.

put.summary: The oracle does not support multipart uploads

400.description: Always: the oracle answers every multipart call 400 bad_request.

get.summary: Serve a blob's content, publicly, no authentication
get.description: The `{pathname+}` greedy label is mirror's spelling of the oracle's `:pathname{.+}`: a blob pathname swallows the rest of the path, separators included.

200.description: The blob's bytes. This schema is an envelope for the bundle, not the wire shape: the wire answer is `body` as the raw response with the other members unfolded into headers.

304.description: if-none-match equalled the blob's ETag; ETag and Cache-Control headers and no body.

UploadResult.description: What the oracle's upload handler answers (its headResponse minus size, cacheControl and uploadedAt).

BlobHead.description: The oracle's headResponse, field for field.

cursor.description: The last pathname of the page; the oracle omits it unless hasMore, and the bundle answers null rather than omitting it.

folders.description: Folded folder prefixes when mode=folded; null otherwise, where the oracle omits the member.

urls.description: Each entry is a blob URL or a bare pathname; entries naming other stores or nothing at all are skipped.

BlobContent.description: Not a wire body: the serving route answers the raw bytes with headers, and this envelope is where a bundle names them. body is the content; not_modified turns the answer into a header-only 304.
